chapter: Starting out in New York and Chicago
title: Billie Holiday at the Grand Terrace and the floor shows
summary: Billie Holiday flopped her first weeks then won everyone, and fainted when told John Dillinger was in the audience. Horace describes the full floor-show productions the band backed.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Billie Holiday as the musicians knew her

blocks.x: A very young lady, and I think her name is familiar -- Lady Day.

Billie Holiday at the Grant Terrace. Do you know her first couple of weeks there, she flopped? That's how square they were in Chicago, they didn't understand her, but after they -- it began to grow on them. She tore it up there, and she won everybody. In fact, I remember one night, we were at the Grant Terrace. This is the Grant Terrace that finally moved from 35th and Giles over to 39th and South Park. This is where Ed Fox moved into a building there. And Billie Holiday --
This was a ball room type.
This was a ball room type, place, yeah.
And Billie Holiday was singing one night, and somebody from the floor mentioned there's John Dillinger sitting out in the audience enjoying it. She fainted.

Right on the floor. Yes. And nobody knew anything, and he got a little carried away, disturbed because of the fact, you know. And his lieutenants were stationed all over there, in the dark, the lights out naturally -- the show's going on. Because in those days, we had a production, you know; when we said floor show, we meant floor show -- opening number, comedians, singers, dancers, a line of girls -- twelve girls, you know. And we had to all those things; [it was easy] with Fletcher play for (unintelligible) because everybody read. We had a producer named Sammy Dyer from Chicago that produced most of the shows, and he died. There was a fella named Joe "Ziggy" Johnson at the Grand Terrace. that produced the shows (unintelligible). And I mean they were productions -- things you don't see now, like in Las Vegas. These are the types of show -- and the costumes -- there were tap dancers, and we had great tap dancers, comedians like Duster Fletcher, was on this thing.
So this is the experience I got in those early years, Tom.
